text_blocks.snippet: The H-1B visa program is undergoing several changes, with a final rule taking effect on January 17, 2025, implementing a beneficiary-centric selection process, start date flexibility, and enhanced integrity measures. These changes include a beneficiary-centric selection process for registrations, codifying start date flexibility, and strengthening program integrity measures. Additionally, the cap-gap extension for eligible F-1 students has been extended from October 1 to April 1 of the relevant fiscal year.
snippet_highlighted_words: implementing a beneficiary-centric selection process, start date flexibility, and enhanced integrity measures

list.snippet: The new rule implements a beneficiary-centric selection process for H-1B registrations, ensuring each beneficiary has an equal chance of selection regardless of the number of registrations submitted by an employer.
The rule codifies existing USCIS policy regarding start dates for H-1B petitions subject to the cap, providing more flexibility for petitioners.
The rule introduces measures to reduce potential fraud and gaming of the registration system.

The cap-gap extension for eligible F-1 students has been extended from October 1 to April 1 of the relevant fiscal year, allowing students to maintain their legal status while waiting for their H-1B petitions to be processed.
The final rule revises the definition of a "specialty occupation" and provides additional protections for certain F-1 students.
USCIS is also launching an online filing option for Forms I-129 (Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker) and Form I-907 (Request for Premium Processing Service) for H-1B petitioners.
The rule eliminates the employer-employee relationship language and expands the definition of a U.S. employer, allowing beneficiary-owned companies to petition for H-1B visas.
The new regulations address remote work for H-1B holders, requiring that job duties align with the original petition and that employers actively monitor the performance of remote workers.
Business owners can now self-petition for an H-1B visa, even if they are the sole owner of their company.
The premium processing fee for H-1B petitions increased from $2,500 to $2,805, according to CDF Labor Law LLP.

text_blocks.snippet: These changes aim to modernize the H-1B program, improve its efficiency, and enhance its integrity.
